MINISTERIAL ORDER N° 005/MoE/25
OF 25/08/2025 RELATING TO AIR
POLLUTANT EMISSION
The Minister of Environment;
Pursuant to the Constitution of the Republic
of Rwanda;
Pursuant to Law n° 18/2016 of 18/05/2016
governing the preservation of air quality and
prevention of air pollution in Rwanda,
especially in Articles 9, 14, 21 and 22;
Having reviewed Ministerial Order n°
02/2018 of 17/09/2018 relating to air
pollutants emission;
After consideration and approval by the
Cabinet, in its meeting of 30/07/2025;
ORDERS:

CHAPTER ONE: GENERAL
PROVISIONS
Article One: Purpose of this Order
This Order determines –
(a) modalities and requirements for
compliance with the permissible
emission limits for means of transport
using petroleum products;
(b) requirements and modalities for
applying, granting and using air
pollutant emission permit;
(c) modalities for notifying air-polluting
activities to the person concerned; and
(d) administrative sanctions for violations
of the law governing the preservation
of air quality and prevention of air
pollution in Rwanda.
Article 2: Interpretation
In this Order:

(a) “District” means a district with legal
personality;
(b) “Authority” means the national
authority in charge of environmental
protection;
(c) “air pollutant emission permit”
means a permit granted by the
Authority to an operator of an air-
polluting activity that does not comply
with the air quality standards.
Article 3: Scope of application
This Order applies to –
(a) all types of emission-generating
motorised means of transport; and
(b) permissible activities that do not
comply with air quality standards.
CHAPTER II: COMPLIANCE WITH
POLLUTANT EMISSION LIMITS

Article 4: Applicable standards
The emission limit standards for pollutants
from emission-generating motorised means of
transport are established by the State organ in
charge of standards.
Article 5: Obligations of the owner or
driver of an emission-generating motorised
means of transport
The owner or driver of an emission-
generating motorised means of transport is
required to maintain the means of transport in
accordance with the best technical practices
to ensure compliance with permissible air
pollutant emission limits.
Article 6: Obligations of the owner or
operator of a machine using petroleum
products
The owner or operator of a machine using
petroleum products is required to service its
engine and maintain the machine in

accordance with the best technical practices
to ensure compliance with permissible air
pollutant emission limits.
Article 7: Requirements for importation of
motorcycles
(1) A motorcycle imported into Rwanda
must be brand new. However, without
prejudice to provisions of other laws,
the Authority, upon request, may
authorize importation of a second-
hand motorcycle if it is designed
either for sports use or for persons
with disabilities.
(2) No person is authorised to import a
two-stroke motorcycle in Rwanda,
except those specifically designed for
sport purposes.
Article 8: Inspection of motorised means of
transport
(1) The Authority inspects emission-
generating motorised means of
transport including motorcycles,
automobile vehicles, and other
machines using petroleum products,

with regard to air pollutant emission.
(2) An emission-generating motorised
means of transport that undergoes and
passes air pollutant emission
inspection must get an inspection
certificate in order to operate.
However, an emission-generating
motorised means of transport that has
not yet been inspected or that has
failed the inspection may be permitted
to move on public highway if –
(a) a motorised means of transport is
being driven from the inspection
centre to a garage;
(b) a motorised means of transport is
being driven from the
impoundment yard to a garage;
(c) a motorised means of transport
is being driven from garage back
to the inspection centre;
(d) a second-hand motorised means of
transport is being driven from the

entry border point to a public or
private warehouse;
(e) a motorised means of transport is
driven from a warehouse to the
inspection centre; or
(f) a motorised means of transport is
transiting through Rwanda or
staying in Rwanda for a period not
exceeding three months; however,
if that stay is extended, the
motorised means of transport must
undergo inspection.
(3) However, a brand new emission-
generating motorised means of
transport that has been in operation
for less than two years is not required
to undergo air pollutant emission
inspection before the expiry of that
time period; however, this exemption
does not apply to second hand-
vehicles.

Article 9: Inspection certificate
(1) The following motorised means of
transport that undergo and pass the air
pollutant emission inspection are
issued an inspection certificate valid
for six months:
(a) motorised means of transport
designed for public transport;
(b) motorised means of transport
designed to carry goods;
(c) training vehicles;
(d) motorised means of transport
licensed for commercial activities;
(e) rescue vehicles;
(f) school buses;
(g) motorised means of transport
using petroleum products designed
for construction, agriculture and

related works;
(h) ambulances;
(2) An inspection certificate for
categories of motorised means of
transport not mentioned in Paragraph
(1) is valid for one year.
(3) A motorised means of transport that
does not pass the air pollutant
emission inspection is not issued an
inspection certificate.
(4) If any defects are identified by the
inspection, the owner of a motorised
means of transport must remedy them
and present it for a further inspection
to certify that the defects have been
corrected prior to issuing the
inspection certificate.
Article 10: Inspection fees
The motorised means of transport owner pays
inspection fees, based on the categories of
motorised means of transport subject to
inspection, as provided for in Annex.

CHAPTER III: APPLICATION, ISSUE
AND USE OF AIR POLLUTANT
EMISSION PERMIT
Article 11: Requirements of application for
air pollutant emission permit
A person who intends to apply for an air
pollutant emission permit to carry out an air
polluting activity and does not comply with
the air quality standards submits a written
application to the Authority, indicating the
following:
(a) identification of the applicant;
(b) description of the air pollutant
activity;
(c) location of the air pollutant activity
covered by the application;
(d) type and origin of the pollutants;
(e) reasons for exceeding air pollutant
emission limits;

(f) expected quantities of air pollutant
emission;
(g) measures put in place to record and
monitor air pollutant emission
quantities;
(h) duration for which the permit is
requested;
(i) other information considered
necessary for appropriate assessment.
Article 12: Application fees for the permit
A person who applies for an air pollutant
emission permit pays a non-refundable fee of
FRW 50,000 to the fund in charge of
environment and climate change.
Article 13: Criteria for assessing the
application for permit
(1) In determining whether to issue an air
pollutant emission permit, the
Authority must –

(a) refer to the report of
environmental impact assessment
or environmental audit conducted;
(b) refer to the applicable ambient air
quality standards;
(c) consider the cumulative effect on
the environment likely to result
from the granting of the permit;
and
(d) ensure that the prescribed best
practicable option is adopted.
(2) The Authority may, if necessary,
require a detailed study to be carried
out at the applicant’s expense before
making a final decision on the permit
application.
Article 14: Response to the application for
air pollutant emission permit
(1) The Authority responds to the
applicant for air pollutant emission

permit within 20 days from the date
on which the applicant submitted all
the required documents.
(2) If additional time to what is provided
for in Paragraph (1) is required for
analysis of the application, the
Authority informs the applicant of the
expected time of issuing the response.
(3) The air pollutant emission permit
indicates the conditions of use with
which the holder must comply.
Article 15: Obligations of a permit holder
A holder of an air pollutant emission permit
must –
(a) conduct continuous monitoring of air
pollutant emissions and implement
other measures to maintain ambient
air quality or improve;
(b) draw up a report on the compliance
status of the air pollutant emission

activity and periodically inform the
Authority thereof; and
(c) comply with conditions specified in
the permit.
Article 16: Validity of the permit
The air pollutant emission permit is valid for
a period of two years from the date of issue
and may be renewed.
Article 17: Permit cancellation
The Authority cancels the air pollutant
emission permit if –
(a) the permit holder fails to comply with
the conditions of use of the air
pollutant emission permit; or
(b) the activity changes location.
Article 18: Notification of the change of the
owner or operator of an activity
(1) The owner or operator of an activity
for which an air pollutant emission

permit is granted notifies the
Authority in writing of the name and
address of the new owner or operator
within 15 days following the
occurrence of change of the owner or
the operator.
(2) The notification must be accompanied
by a written commitment from the
new owner or operator of the activity
to comply with the conditions of the
existing air pollutant emission permit.
A copy of the notification is sent to
the City of Kigali or relevant District.
Article 19: Change of a pollutant-emitting
activity
(1) The owner or operator of an activity
who holds an air pollutant emission
permit notifies the Authority in
writing of the change of the pollutant-
emitting activity within 15 days prior
to the change of the activity.
(2) If the new pollutant-emitting activity
results in air pollutant emissions that

exceed permissible emission limits,
the owner or operator of the activity
applies for an air pollutant emission
permit as provided for in this Order.
Article 20: Fees for air pollutant emission
(1) A person who is granted an air
pollutant emission permit pays annual
fees to the fund in charge of
environment and climate change.
(2) The Authority sets and publishes
annually the applicable fee rates for
air pollutant emissions.
CHAPTER IV: NOTIFICATION OF AIR-
POLLUTING ACTIVITY AND APPEAL
AGAINST THE NOTIFICATION
Article 21: Notification of air-polluting
activity
(1) The City of Kigali or the District with

legal personality notifies in writing
the owner of an activity that their
activity pollutes the air.
(2) A notice of air-polluting activity must
specify the following:
(a) the type of violation being cited;
(b) the measures required to prevent
emissions or ensure compliance
with emission limits;
(c) the period within which measures
referred to under subparagraph (b)
must be taken;
(d) the reporting schedule for the
implementation status of measures
taken.
Article 22: Appeal against notification
(1) A person to whom a notification of
air-polluting activity has been served,
within two working days of its receipt,
may lodge an appeal in writing with
the City of Kigali or the District that

issued the notification.
(2) A person served with the notification
of air-polluting activity who is not
satisfied with the decision on their
appeal, within two working days from
the date of receipt of the decision,
may submit a written appeal to the
Authority regarding the terms of the
notification.
(3) The Authority, after considering the
appeal, may confirm, amend or revoke
the notification of air-polluting
activity. The Authority informs in
writing the appellant and the City of
Kigali or the District of the decision
taken within 15 days after submission
of the filing of the appeal.
(4) The appellant pays FRW 50,000 to the
fund in charge of environment and
climate change before lodging their
appeal. This amount is refunded to the
appellant if the Authority upholds
their appeal.

Article 23: Content of the appeal file
against the notice of air-polluting activity
The appeal file against a notice of air-
polluting activity must contain the following:
(a) a duly signed appeal petition;
(b) a copy of the decision being appealed;
(c) proof of payment of the appeal fee;
(d) any other relevant document
considered necessary.
CHAPTER V: FAULTS AND
SANCTIONS
Article 24: Violation of air-pollutant
emission standards
(1) A person, other than the driver of a
motorised means of transport, who
violates air pollutant emission
standards commits a fault and is liable
to a fine of FRW 3,000,000.

(2) The owner of a motorised means of
transport that fails to comply with air
pollutant emission standards commits
a fault and is liable to a fine of FRW
25,000.
Article 25: Engaging in air polluting
activity without permit
A person who carries out an air-polluting
activity that does not comply with applicable
air quality standards without a permit
commits a fault and is liable to a fine of FRW
3,000,000.
Article 26: Violation of a compliance order
related to preservation of air quality
A person who violates a compliance order
relating to the preservation of air quality and
prevention of air pollution commits a fault
and is liable to a fine of FRW 2,000,000.

Article 27: Violation of an order to cease
activities
A person who violates an order to cease air
polluting activities commits a fault and is
liable to a fine of FRW 5,000,000.
Article 28: Violation of orders for
emergency prevention of the emission of
air pollutants
A person who violates an order for
emergency prevention of emission of air
pollutants commits a fault and is liable to a
fine of FRW 3,000,000.
Article 29: Hindrance to inspection
A person who –
(a) obstructs an environmental inspector
in the execution of their duties;
(b) refuses an environmental inspector
entry onto land or into premises for
purposes of inspection;
(c) refuses an environmental inspector

access to records kept in accordance
with the law; or
(d) provides an environmental inspector
with a false name, false address, or
misleading information;
commits a fault and is liable to a fine of FRW
500,000.
Article 30: Failure to report accidental or
involuntary emission of air pollutants
A person who fails to report an accidental or
involuntary emission of air pollutants within
the time prescribed by law commits a fault
and is liable to a fine of FRW 1,000,000.
Article 31: Remedial measures
(1) The Authority, the City of Kigali or
the District with legal personality may
order a person who violates provisions
of the law relating to the preservation
of air quality and prevention of air
pollution –

(a) to remove, repair, remediate,
or upgrade the source of
pollution; or
(b) to restore the environment
damaged or destroyed by air
pollutants.
(2) If provisions of Paragraph (1) are not
complied with, the Authority, the City
of Kigali or the District with legal
personality may order the temporary
or permanent closure of the activity
concerned.
Article 32: Fine payment period
A person sanctioned with the payment of
fines under this Chapter, pays the fine to the
fund in charge of environment and climate
change, within seven days from the receipt of
the notification. If this period elapses without
payment, the person pays an additional
charge of zero point five percent for each day
of delay.

Article 33: Competent organs to impose
fine
The fine provided for in this Order is imposed
by the Authority, the City of Kigali or the
District with legal personality. However, the
fine related to emissions from motorised
means of transport is imposed by Rwanda
National Police.
CHAPTER VI: MISCELLANEOUS AND
FINAL PROVISIONS
Article 34: Motorcycle already in Rwanda
on the date of entry into force of this Order
A motorcycle already in Rwanda on the date
of entry into force of this Order continues to
operate. However, it must comply with
provisions of this Order regarding permissible
air pollutant emission limits.
Article 35: Validity of a permit issued
before the entry into force of this Order
Air pollutant emission permit issued before
the entry into force of this Order remains
valid until its expiration.

Article 35: Language provision
This Order was drafted in Ikinyarwanda.
Article 37: Repealing provision
Ministerial Order n° 02/2018 of 17/09/2018
relating to air pollutants emission is repealed.
Article 38: Entry into force
This Order comes into force on the date of its
publication in the Official Gazette of the
Republic of Rwanda.

Kigali, 25/08/2025
